stories.title: Murray 42, Jokic Triple-Double Power Nuggets Past Pelicans 141-135 OT
stories.angle: Murray erupts for 42 points (8-of-16 from three) and Jokic posts his 199th career triple-double (35/15/10) as Denver rallies from 23 down to win in OT

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Down 23. Murray said no.

42 points, 8 threes, OT win. Jokic added 35/15/10 for his 199th career triple-double.

Nuggets 141, Pelicans 135. That's Denver basketball. #DenverNuggets

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Nikola Jokic's 199th career triple-double.

35 pts. 15 reb. 10 ast. And it still needed Murray's 42 to seal it in overtime.

The Big Fella just keeps going. #DenverNuggets

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:30 PM ET

Denver just pulled off one of the early season's most stunning comebacks.

Down 23 points in the third quarter, the Nuggets looked finished. The Pelicans were rolling, leading 73-57 at halftime and extending their lead entering the fourth. Then something switched.

Jamal Murray turned into a one-man wrecking crew — 42 points, 8 threes, and clutch free throws when they mattered most. Nikola Jokic added a 35/15/10 masterpiece — his 199th career regular-season triple-double. Combined, the two stars put up 77 points. And rookie Trevon Brazile stepped up with 7 huge points in overtime to seal it in his home debut.

Final: Nuggets 141, Pelicans 135 in OT.

This is why you never count Denver out. The Nuggets have made a habit of digging deep, and Saturday night they did it again — in spectacular fashion.

article.headline: Murray 42, Jokic 35/15/10: Nuggets Stun Pelicans 141-135 in OT After 23-Point Hole

stories.title: Booker Sets Suns Home Opener Record with 43 as Warriors Fall to 0-3
stories.angle: Booker shoots 17-of-25 (43 pts, 7 reb, 7 ast) to set a Phoenix franchise record for most points in a home opener; shorthanded Warriors drop to 0-3

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Devin Booker just rewrote the Suns' home opener record book.

43 points. 17-for-25. 7 rebounds. 7 assists. Warriors had no answer.

Suns 131, Warriors 122. #Suns

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Curry. Green. Podziemski. Horford. All rested.

Warriors fall to 0-3 after Suns blowout.

The early-season hole is getting deeper in Golden State. #DubNation

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:30 PM ET

Devin Booker had a message for the Phoenix Suns faithful on Saturday night, and he delivered it in record-breaking fashion.

43 points — the most any Suns player has ever posted in a home opener. 17-for-25 from the field. Seven rebounds and seven assists. A near triple-double that had the Footprint Center absolutely rocking.

The Warriors were shorthanded — Stephen Curry, Draymond Green, Brandin Podziemski, and Al Horford all sat out — but Booker and the Suns didn't care. After a rough opening-night loss at Portland, Phoenix sent a clear message on Saturday: they're here, and Booker is locked in.

Golden State drops to 0-3. A quiet start to the season is turning into a concerning one for the Warriors.

Final: Suns 131, Warriors 122.

article.headline: Booker Sets Suns Home Opener Record with 43 as Shorthanded Warriors Fall to 0-3

stories.title: Wembanyama 23, Spurs Route Mavericks 122-106 in Texas Showdown
stories.angle: Wembanyama leads Spurs past struggling Mavericks; Dallas continues rocky start to 2026-27

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Wembanyama with 23 points. Spurs roll past the Mavericks 122-106.

San Antonio looks dangerous early in 2026-27, and Dallas still searching for answers. #GoSpursGo #MFFL

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:30 PM ET

Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs are making a statement early in 2026-27.

Wembanyama racked up 23 points Saturday as the Spurs handled the Dallas Mavericks 122-106 in a Texas rivalry matchup. San Antonio looked sharp from start to finish — and Wembanyama's two-way brilliance was at the center of it.

Meanwhile, Dallas continues to search for its identity in the early going. The Mavericks are a team expected to compete in the West, but the early results haven't shown it yet. Head coach Jason Kidd and his staff will be studying the film and demanding better.

The Texas showdown goes decisively to San Antonio tonight.

stories.title: Embiid 28, 76ers 127 Bucks 116 — Philly Stays Hot; Durant 22 Rockets Win
stories.angle: Embiid drops 28 as Philly keeps pace in East; KD leads Rockets past Hawks 121-114

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Joel Embiid drops 28. 76ers beat the Bucks 127-116 to stay hot early.

Philly is clicking, and the East better take notice. #Sixers

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

Saturday's NBA slate was packed with quality performances from start to finish.

Joel Embiid dropped 28 to lead the 76ers past the Bucks 127-116. Philly is clicking, and the Eastern Conference better take notice. Kevin Durant scored 22 as the Rockets beat the Hawks 121-114. Brandon Miller had a massive night for Charlotte, scoring 34 to lead the Hornets past the Heat 115-110 in one of the more impressive individual performances of the young season.

The Cavaliers held off the Nets 125-121, and the Wizards edged the Bulls 124-120 — Coby Wilson put up 30 in a losing effort for Chicago, a promising sign for a young Bulls team building toward something.

Eight games, eight storylines. The 2026-27 season is delivering.
